name: Treaty with the Creeks, 1805 (first Treaty of Washington)
promises: Article 1: the Creeks ceded the land between the Oconee and Ocmulgee rivers but kept title and possession of a tract five miles long and three wide at the old Ocmulgee fields, where the President could keep a military post and trading house.
Article 2: the United States gained a right to a horse path through Creek country from the Ocmulgee to Mobile, with the Creeks to keep boats and houses of entertainment along it.

Article 3: for the land, the path and the post, the United States would pay twelve thousand dollars a year for eight years and eleven thousand dollars a year for the ten years after, in money, goods or farm implements as the Creeks chose.
Article 4: two blacksmiths and two strikers for eight years.
today: No Indian Claims Commission, Court of Claims or other federal finding about this cession or its annuities was found in this pass. The Inter-Tribal Council of the Five Civilized Tribes (Resolution 2002-18) says the treaty excluded the Ocmulgee Old Fields reserve tract from the cession and that Muscogee people were later forced to cede all their Georgia lands through subsequent treaties.

nationVoice.nation: Inter-Tribal Council of the Five Civilized Tribes (of which the Muscogee (Creek) Nation is a member)
nationVoice.summary: The Council says Article 1 of this treaty kept the Ocmulgee Old Fields "Reserve Tract" out of the cession, that the Muscogee were later forced to cede all their Georgia lands, and it affirms the Old Fields as a Muscogee traditional cultural property.

sources.title: Treaty with the Creeks, 1805 (Kappler, Indian Affairs: Laws and Treaties, vol. 2)

Inter-Tribal Council of the Five Civilized Tribes, Resolution 2002-18 (Ocmulgee Old Fields as a Muscogee traditional cultural property)
sources.publisher: Inter-Tribal Council of the Five Civilized Tribes

openQuestions: Whether all eighteen annual payments under Article 3 were made was not traced; the Creek dockets in the Indian Claims Commission collection (21, 167, 168, 169, 273 to 276, 280, 292) do not appear to cover this cession.
The Ocmulgee reserve tract kept by Article 1 passed out of Creek hands under a later treaty; that loss belongs to the later treaty's record.
The Muscogee (Creek) Nation's own published account of this treaty was not found in this pass; the Inter-Tribal Council resolution is the closest.
